_comment: The movement patterns the Form Coach can judge, and the rules that map a
catalog row onto one. Projected into the catalog as `poseTargetId`.
A pattern is NOT an exercise. A back squat, a front squat, a goblet squat
and an air squat are one silhouette seen from the side, so they share one
hand-authored target. That is why the authoring cost is paid per pattern
and the coverage is counted per exercise.
`excludeWhen` is the same list for every pattern on purpose: what makes a
movement unjudgeable by one side-on camera is the same in each case --
a machine or bench that hides the hip line, or a seated/lying position in
which the shoulder-hip-knee chain means nothing. BlazePose has no spinal
landmark at any configuration, which is what already forced two rules to
be silenced (see form_classifier.dart); nothing here can recover it.

patterns.label: Squat
_notTitleWhy: `squatTopTarget`/`squatBottomTarget` encode ONE thing: a bilateral,
upright squat seen from the side. Everything below carries the word
'squat' and is not that, so the target would score a correct rep
badly -- and this is the only pattern the coach currently supports,
so every false positive here reaches a user immediately.
split stance      split squat, bulgarian -- the lunge silhouette.
Without this they matched two patterns and the
ambiguity rule dropped all 40, which was correct
behaviour applied to a question that was never
ambiguous. Handled per pattern rather than by a
global precedence order, because 'Alternating
Plank Lunge' really IS ambiguous and a precedence
rule would have silently resolved that one too.
not sagittal      side, lateral, curtsy, cossack, skater -- these
happen across the frontal plane, which a side-on
camera sees edge-on.
not bilateral     pistol, single leg, sissy -- a different shape,
and the target's two legs are drawn together.
not upright       kneeling, jefferson.
isometric         squat hold, wall squat: RepCounter needs a full
lap of the phase ladder, and a hold never leaves
the bottom. No reps, nothing to score.
two movements     squat + press/row/raise/reach/punch/kick/burpee.
One silhouette cannot judge two movements.
false friend      'Barbell Incline Shoulders Press (inside Squat
Cage)' is not a squat at all -- the word is in
the equipment's name. Caught by 'squat cage'.
Deliberately NOT excluded: 'Squat to Grass' (a depth cue, not a
second movement), 'with 2 Sec Hold' and 'with Rack' (a paused squat
still completes a lap), and sumo. Sumo from the side is imperfect --
the knees splay away from the camera -- but it is a judgement call
worth making with a measurement rather than a guess.
patterns.notTitle: split squat|bulgarian|side squat|lateral squat|curtsy|cossack|skater|sissy|pistol|single leg|kneeling|jefferson|squat cage|squat row|squat hold|wall squat|burpee|\bpress\b|\brow\b|\braise\b|\breach\b|punch|kick|heel touch|squat to (front|side)

patterns.label: Hip hinge
_matchTitleWhy: `hip thrust` and `glute bridge` were in this list and are gone. They
ARE a hip hinge at the joint, which is why someone put them here --
but a tag claims the SILHOUETTE seen from the side is this pattern,
and both are performed supine while the hinge target draws a standing
deadlift. The rule had conflated the joint action with the shape.
43 rows, the largest single group this gate removes.
Removed from `matchTitle` rather than cancelled by a `notTitle`:
cancelling a token this file itself chose to match would leave the
mistake on the page with a correction stapled underneath it.

patterns.label: Lunge and split stance
_matchTitleWhy: `step[- ]?up` was in this list and is gone. A step-up RISES onto a
platform; the lunge target drops one knee toward the floor from
standing. Opposite vertical direction, and the platform the movement
depends on is not in the drawing at all. 7 rows.
'Dumbbell Rear Lunge From Step' keeps its tag and should: it matches
`\blunge`, and it is a lunge that happens to begin on a step.

patterns.label: Push-up and plank
_notTitleWhy: A side plank lies on ONE side, supported on a forearm, with the
shoulder-hip-ankle line rolled ninety degrees out of the push-up and
front-plank shape this pattern draws. A side-on camera sees that
shape edge-on -- the same reason `squat` excludes lateral, curtsy and
cossack work.
Seven rows already carried this tag and were wrong. Nothing offers
`pushup` to a user today, and that is deliberately not the test: a tag
asserts what the silhouette IS, not what the coach can score, so the
tag stays valid for the day the pattern becomes coachable. See this
file's sibling module header. Found by GPT-PM reviewing this gate's
own plan -- the pass that wrote the original rule missed it, and so
did the first two revisions of the plan to fix it.

patterns.label: Standing curl
_notTitleWhy: A wrist curl moves the wrist and holds the elbow still. Elbow flexion
is the entire signal the curl target scores, so it would read a
correct wrist curl as a rep that never began. 11 rows.
`leg curl` needs no rule here -- the shared `excludeWhen` already drops
it, and for the right reason: it is done lying on a machine.

patterns.label: Sit-up and crunch
_notTitleWhy: Three shapes that are not a sagittal curl-up. 11 rows.
oblique / twist   rotation and lateral flexion cross the frontal and
transverse planes, which a side-on camera sees
edge-on -- the same reason `squat` drops curtsy
and cossack variants.
hollow hold       a hold. RepCounter needs a full lap of the phase
ladder, and a hold never leaves the top.
`hanging` is deliberately NOT a rule: the one hanging row here is
'Hanging Oblique Crunches', already caught by `oblique`. A rule that
fires on nothing is a claim with no evidence under it.

excludeWhen.title: seated|lying|\bbench\b|machine|smith|cable|lat pull|leg press|leg extension|leg curl|pec deck|hack squat|assisted|sled|ergometer
